gh pr create --base main --title "Issue unlinkable SD-JWT VCs: dc+sd-jwt, Token Status List, batch issuance" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## Why

Unlinkability is a core requirement for VeriCred from v1: if one person shows a credential to two verifiers, the verifiers must not be able to tell it was the same person. VeriCred's credentials didn't meet that. Every credential carried values that stay the same across presentations: the holder key (`cnf`), `sub`, an exact `iat`, and a sequential status index.

It also didn't meet the German EUDI ecosystem's EAA issuance guidance, which requires a **Token Status List** for SD-JWT VC and the `dc+sd-jwt` format.

## What changed

- **`dc+sd-jwt`:** the JWT header `typ` now matches the configured format (default `dc+sd-jwt`, was `vc+sd-jwt`).
- **IETF Token Status List replaces W3C StatusList2021.** Credentials carry `status.status_list: { idx, uri }`. `/status/{listId}` serves a signed `statuslist+jwt` with a ZLIB-compressed 1-bit list, as `application/statuslist+jwt`.
- **Random status index per credential**, not sequential, so list positions don't reveal issuance order or group batch copies.
- **OID4VCI 1.0 batch issuance:** a `proofs.jwt` array returns `credentials[]`, one copy per holder key. It's advertised as `batch_credential_issuance.batch_size` (default 10, set via `credential.batchSize`). The single-`proof` request still works.
- **Unlinkability hardening:**
  - `iat` and `exp` are rounded down to the UTC day.
  - Each copy gets fresh salts and its own pairwise `sub`.
  - A batch that reuses one key is rejected with `invalid_proof`.
- **Batch revocation:** revoking one copy revokes the whole batch. The `batchId` is stored only on the issuer side and never appears in the credential.
- Docs updated: AGENTS.md, README, wallet interop guide, and the decision table in implementation_plan_v2.

## Tests

- New: `src/oid4vci/__tests__/unlinkable-batch.test.ts`. It issues a batch and asserts that the copies share no value apart from issuer, type, day-rounded timestamps, the status list URI and `_sd_alg`. It also covers key reuse, a batch larger than `batch_size`, and batch revocation through the Token Status List.
- Updated the existing status list, revocation and interop tests to the new format.
- With `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism`: **199 of 202 pass**. The 3 failures also fail on `main` on Windows: `auth-bypass` gets a 404 for the landing page, and the two `path-containment` tests assume Unix paths.
- In the default parallel run, results vary between runs because existing test files use the same server ports (3514, 3516, 3517). That also happens on `main`.

## Breaking change

Credentials issued before this change reference StatusList2021 at the same URL, so their revocation check no longer works. VeriCred is still v0.1, so we accept this; those credentials need to be reissued.

## Not covered yet

- Issuance with a real wallet in the German EUDI sandbox (EUDI reference wallet). That's the next validation step.
- The age template's `age_attested_at` disclosure is date-granular. Disclosing it reveals no more than the day-rounded `iat`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

- **Random status index per credential**, not sequential, so list positions don't reveal issuance order or group batch copies.
- **OID4VCI 1.0 batch issuance:** a `proofs.jwt` array returns `credentials[]`, one copy per holder key. It's advertised as `batch_credential_issuance.batch_size` (default 10, set via `credential.batchSize`). The single-`proof` request still works.
- **Unlinkability hardening:**
  - `iat` and `exp` are rounded down to the UTC day.
  - Each copy gets fresh salts and its own pairwise `sub`.
  - A batch that reuses one key is rejected with `invalid_proof`.
- **Batch revocation:** revoking one copy revokes the whole batch. The `batchId` is stored only on the issuer side and never appears in the credential.
- Docs updated: AGENTS.md, README, wallet interop guide, and the decision table in implementation_plan_v2.

## Tests

- New: `src/oid4vci/__tests__/unlinkable-batch.test.ts`. It issues a batch and asserts that the copies share no value apart from issuer, type, day-rounded timestamps, the status list URI and `_sd_alg`. It also covers key reuse, a batch larger than `batch_size`, and batch revocation through the Token Status List.
- Updated the existing status list, revocation and interop tests to the new format.
- With `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism`: **199 of 202 pass**. The 3 failures also fail on `main` on Windows: `auth-bypass` gets a 404 for the landing page, and the two `path-containment` tests assume Unix paths.
- In the default parallel run, results vary between runs because existing test files use the same server ports (3514, 3516, 3517). That also happens on `main`.

## Breaking change

Credentials issued before this change reference StatusList2021 at the same URL, so their revocation check no longer works. VeriCred is still v0.1, so we accept this; those credentials need to be reissued.

## Not covered yet

- Issuance with a real wallet in the German EUDI sandbox (EUDI reference wallet). That's the next validation step.
- The age template's `age_attested_at` disclosure is date-granular. Disclosing it reveals no more than the day-rounded `iat`.

content.text: what are the next steps for the sandbox wallet test

Here are the next steps, in order. The first two can start today. Which items come from the German guide and which are my assumptions is labelled.

## 1. Apply for access (your part, takes the longest)
- **Pick one use case**, for example "membership credential for association X". The guide requires one intent form per use case, and access is "only possible with a clearly defined use case."
- **Submit the intent form** on [eudi-wallet.gov.de](https://eudi-wallet.gov.de/en/ecosystem-knowledge-center) and sign up for the **monthly kick-off call**. After that you get the closed beta wallet and the sandbox registrar for certificates.
- **Open question:** whether you can apply as an individual, without an organization. The guide asks for "a digital service that requires user verification." Ask directly in the form.

## 2. Make VeriCred reachable (can start now)
- **A public HTTPS URL** that actually points to your VeriCred instance, either a domain or a tunnel such as ngrok or Cloudflare Tunnel.
- **Issuer URL in the config = that URL.** This is the `thatthing.de` vs `localhost` mismatch from the beginning. The wallet only talks to what the metadata says.
- I can build the **setup-time URL check** from earlier (VeriCred fetches its own metadata from that URL) so this can't silently break again.

## 3. Likely technical gap: issuer certificate (my assumption, not checked against the guide)
VeriCred identifies itself through `did:web` and a key ID. EUDI wallets usually expect an **X.509 certificate chain (`x5c`) in the credential header**, signed by the sandbox registrar. That's why the registrar exists. If that's right, VeriCred needs:
- to accept a key and certificate issued by the registrar,
- and to put `x5c` in the header of every credential and status list.

Check this before writing code, in the guide pages we haven't read yet (the HAIP example flow and the lifecycle page). I can do that research now.

## 4. Register the credential type
Register the `vct` (for example `MembershipCredential`) as an entry in the sandbox catalog, and write a short **rulebook**: fields, batch size, revocation within 24h, no fixed `sub`.

## 5. Run the test and keep evidence
Scan the offer with the beta wallet → receive a **batch** → present the credential to a sandbox verifier → revoke → present again, which must fail. Record wallet version, date and screenshots in the repo. Only then switch the interop guide to "✅ Tested".

**My suggestion for right now:** you start step 1 (intent form) today. I research the certificate question from step 3, so we know whether that code is needed before access arrives. Should I start that research?

content.text:
An automated security review flagged one point in the commit I just pushed. I agree with it, and it's more serious than how I described it in the PR.

**The problem:** credentials issued before this change still point to the same `/status/{listId}` URL, but that URL now returns the new Token Status List format. I described the result as "their revocation check no longer works." In fact it depends on the verifier:
- a **strict** verifier rejects the credential. That's safe.
- a **lenient** verifier that finds no revocation bit in the old format treats the credential as **valid**. A credential you revoked earlier would then be accepted again (fail-open).

**How much it matters:** it only affects instances that already issued real credentials before this change, and those expire after at most 30 days by default. Whether your running instance (`thatthing.de`) issued real credentials, I don't know.

**Fix (small, same PR):** existing installations keep their old list ID, which keeps serving StatusList2021 until the last old credential expires. New credentials get a new list ID in the new format. That's about 40 lines plus a test. Then nothing old fails open, and nothing new changes.

Two questions:
1. **Should I add this fix to PR #57?** I recommend it.
2. **And should I then start researching the issuer certificate question (`x5c`) for the sandbox?**

input.old_string:
## Breaking change

Credentials issued before this change reference StatusList2021 at the same URL, so their revocation check no longer works. VeriCred is still v0.1, so we accept this; those credentials need to be reissued.
input.new_string:
## Existing credentials (migration)

Credentials issued before this change reference a W3C StatusList2021 at `/status/{oldListId}`. If that URL served the new format, a lenient verifier could read the missing StatusList2021 bit as "valid" and accept credentials that were already revoked (fail-open).

To prevent that, an existing store is migrated on first load:
- The old list ID stays as `legacyListId` and is **still served as StatusList2021**, including revocations made after the migration.
- New credentials go to a **fresh** Token Status List ID.
- A store with no issued credentials just switches format, since nothing references the old URL.

Covered by `keeps serving a migrated legacy list as StatusList2021 so revocations never fail open` in `src/revocation/__tests__/statuslist.test.ts`. Credentials that already exist keep working until they expire, so no reissue is needed.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
## Why

Unlinkability is a core requirement for VeriCred from v1: if one person shows a credential to two verifiers, the verifiers must not be able to tell it was the same person. VeriCred's credentials didn't meet that. Every credential carried values that stay the same across presentations: the holder key (`cnf`), `sub`, an exact `iat`, and a sequential status index.

It also didn't meet the German EUDI ecosystem's EAA issuance guidance, which requires a **Token Status List** for SD-JWT VC and the `dc+sd-jwt` format.

## What changed

- **`dc+sd-jwt`:** the JWT header `typ` now matches the configured format (default `dc+sd-jwt`, was `vc+sd-jwt`).
- **IETF Token Status List replaces W3C StatusList2021.** Credentials carry `status.status_list: { idx, uri }`. `/status/{listId}` serves a signed `statuslist+jwt` with a ZLIB-compressed 1-bit list, as `application/statuslist+jwt`.
- **Random status index per credential**, not sequential, so list positions don't reveal issuance order or group batch copies.
- **OID4VCI 1.0 batch issuance:** a `proofs.jwt` array returns `credentials[]`, one copy per holder key. It's advertised as `batch_credential_issuance.batch_size` (default 10, set via `credential.batchSize`). The single-`proof` request still works.
- **Unlinkability hardening:**
  - `iat` and `exp` are rounded down to the UTC day.
  - Each copy gets fresh salts and its own pairwise `sub`.
  - A batch that reuses one key is rejected with `invalid_proof`.
- **Batch revocation:** revoking one copy revokes the whole batch. The `batchId` is stored only on the issuer side and never appears in the credential.
- Docs updated: AGENTS.md, README, wallet interop guide, and the decision table in implementation_plan_v2.

## Tests

- New: `src/oid4vci/__tests__/unlinkable-batch.test.ts`. It issues a batch and asserts that the copies share no value apart from issuer, type, day-rounded timestamps, the status list URI and `_sd_alg`. It also covers key reuse, a batch larger than `batch_size`, and batch revocation through the Token Status List.
- Updated the existing status list, revocation and interop tests to the new format.
- With `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism`: **199 of 202 pass**. The 3 failures also fail on `main` on Windows: `auth-bypass` gets a 404 for the landing page, and the two `path-containment` tests assume Unix paths.
- In the default parallel run, results vary between runs because existing test files use the same server ports (3514, 3516, 3517). That also happens on `main`.

## Breaking change

Credentials issued before this change reference StatusList2021 at the same URL, so their revocation check no longer works. VeriCred is still v0.1, so we accept this; those credentials need to be reissued.

## Not covered yet

- Issuance with a real wallet in the German EUDI sandbox (EUDI reference wallet). That's the next validation step.
- The age template's `age_attested_at` disclosure is date-granular. Disclosing it reveals no more than the day-rounded `iat`.

input.prompt:
Question: In the German EUDI Wallet sandbox, how must an EAA issuer (OID4VCI, SD-JWT VC format "dc+sd-jwt") identify its signing key so the German wallet accepts the credential? Specifically: must the issuer-signed JWT header carry an X.509 certificate chain in `x5c` (and issued by whom — the "German EUDI Ecosystem Sandbox Registrar")? Or is `kid` with JWKS at /.well-known/jwt-vc-issuer, or did:web, accepted? Same question for the Token Status List JWT (statuslist+jwt) signing key.

Read these pages (follow links from them to sibling pages under the same developer-guide as needed, e.g. example flows "HAIP", "low-fidelity", the EAA lifecycle page, the sandbox registrar / certificates pages, issuer metadata, "access certificate"/"registration certificate"):
- https://bmi.usercontent.opencode.de/eudi-wallet/developer-guide/eaa/guide/issuance/eaa_issuance/  (read the WHOLE page including the tail past 40k chars; search for x5c, certificate, kid, jwt-vc-issuer, did, trust, signed_metadata, key attestation, wallet attestation)
- https://bmi.usercontent.opencode.de/eudi-wallet/developer-guide/eaa/onboarding/overview/
- https://sandbox.eudi-wallet.org/ (registrar — what certificates it issues: access certificate / issuer signing certificate / for which roles)
- If useful: OpenID4VC High Assurance Interoperability Profile (HAIP) 1.0 at https://openid.net/specs/openid4vc-high-assurance-interoperability-profile-1_0.html — section on SD-JWT VC issuer key resolution (x5c requirement).

Report: (1) exact requirement for issuer credential signing key identification (x5c vs kid/jwks vs did), with verbatim quotes under 125 chars and URLs; (2) who issues the certificate and how to obtain it in the sandbox (CSR? key algorithm P-256? validity?); (3) any requirement for the Token Status List signing (same key/cert? x5c?); (4) any requirement for signed issuer metadata, wallet/key attestation, or issuer authentication of the wallet that an issuer must implement for the sandbox; (5) anything about whether did:web is accepted or not. Clearly mark what the pages do NOT say and which pages you could not read.

content.text:
PR #57 is updated (commit `21e3a5a`). Now the `x5c` result.

## Result: `x5c` research

**Short version: very likely needed, but not stated explicitly in the German guide.**

**What the German guide says:**
- Trust is **certificate-based**: "Use certificates linked to your trust anchor", plus a trust list of "authorized issuers and their certificates".
- Signature algorithm in the metadata template: **ES256**, which VeriCred already uses.
- **Not mentioned at all:** `x5c`, `kid`, `did:web`, or which body issues the certificate.
- The sandbox registrar (`sandbox.eudi-wallet.org`) only loads as an app shell and couldn't be read automatically.

**What HAIP 1.0 says** (the EU's high-assurance profile, which the German guide lists as an example profile, "not mandatory"):
- An SD-JWT VC **MUST** carry the issuer's signing certificate plus its chain in the `x5c` header. It must not be self-signed, and the trust anchor itself is left out.
- **The same applies to the Token Status List.**
- Every credential needs "its own unique, unpredictable status list index". ✅ We built exactly that today.

**What that means for VeriCred:** it identifies itself only through `did:web` and `kid`. A wallet that, like the German one, trusts certificates finds **no certificate it can check** in our credentials. `did:web` doesn't appear anywhere in the German pages, either as allowed or as rejected.

## Other gaps found (from HAIP)
| Point | HAIP | German guide | VeriCred |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x5c` on credential and status list | required | implied | ❌ |
| Nonce endpoint | required | `c_nonce` in the token response is "sufficient" | ✅ for Germany |
| Wallet attestation (client authentication) | issuer must require it | not mentioned | ❌, later |
| Random status index | required | – | ✅ |

## My recommendation
**Build `x5c` support now, as an option.** If the issuer configures a certificate chain, every credential and the status list carry `x5c`. Otherwise everything stays as it is. The key stays with the issuer, as agreed earlier. There's little risk of wasted work: HAIP requires it and the German trust model is built on certificates.

**What only you can find out:** how the registrar issues the certificate (does it need a certificate signing request, and what validity period). That should come from the kick-off call or by looking at `sandbox.eudi-wallet.org` in your browser yourself.
